title: Internal Lateral Reboard — 7d integrator kit
content:
Purpose and scope
This is a lightweight 7-day reboarding kit for engineers and managers who are moving laterally inside Redwood (internal transfer / role pivot). Designed to be used when someone moves teams but does NOT need full new-hire access provisioning (most infra and cloud accounts remain same). Focus: reduce cognitive load, surface knowledge gaps fast, create evidence for a 30-day role-acceptance check-in.

Use cases
- Senior engineer -> platform product engineer (same org, new team)
- IC -> technical program manager (role pivot)
- Contractor conversion where scope slightly shifts

Core principles (fast, evidence-led, async-friendly)
- 7 days to reach signal (not full ramp).
- Prefer async artifacts over long meetings: reading path, runbooks, key PRs.
- Short live syncs only where blockers exist.
- Manager owns outcome, peer mentor owns context.

7-day schedule (owner notes inline)
Day 0 (prestart, manager):
- Confirm role scope doc + 3 priority deliverables for first 30 days (1-pager).
- Set calendar: 30/60/90 check-ins, daily 15-min for first week optional.
- Assign a peer mentor and folder with 5 canonical links.
- README to read: team roadmap, current oncall rotations, open PRs list.
Day 1 (orientation):
- 9:00 intro sync (manager) — 30 min: expectations + immediate priorities.
- 11:00 mentor deep-dive — 45 min: codebase map + recent postmortem.
- Complete access sanity checklist (can access repos, CI, infra dashboards).
- Quick 1-line "I can run" check: run the test suite subset / open a staged dashboard.
Day 2 (context & hands-on):
- Pair with mentor on one small triage / bugfix (goal: commit + merge).
- Read two design docs flagged by mentor.
- Fill first-day evidence log (see Evidence template).
Day 3 (stakeholder mapping):
- Asynchronous stakeholder list (who to ping for X) — share in doc.
- 1:1s scheduled with two cross-functional partners.
- Start a 3-day micro-project: reproduce a flaky test / run a deploy in staging.
Day 4 (deliverable focus):
- Work on micro-project, aim for PR draft.
- Manager feedback loop: 20-min sync for alignment.
Day 5 (quality signal):
- PR submitted + peer review from mentor.
- Runbook updates: add one short improvement to a README.
Day 6 (handoff & docs):
- Complete evidence log.
- Final review with manager: confirm 3-week plan and risk areas.
Day 7 (wrap & check-in):
- 30-min retrospective: what is still unclear, what helped most.
- Submit role-acceptance note (yes/no/conditional) for the 30-day check.

Evidence log (one-paragraph entries; kept on candidate doc)
- Day / Activity / Outcome / Notes on who reviewed.
- Example: "Day 2 — triaged flaky job X, reproduced locally, added fix that reduced failure rate from 8% -> 0% in local test. PR #246 by Priya; reviewed by Maya."

Access sanity checklist (quick)
- Repo read: yes/no
- Repo write (PR): yes/no
- CI pipelines run: yes/no
- Staging deploy permissions: yes/no
- Dashboard access (Grafana/Datadog): yes/no
- Pager access (if oncall): yes/no

Interview & peer-evaluation rubric (for internal acceptance / converting contractors)
Purpose: lightweight peer rubric used during the 7-day micro-project to capture signals. Aim for behavioral + skills + team fit. Use 1–5 scale and a short comment.
Rubric fields (short):
- Problem decomposition (1–5): how they break down unknowns.
- Code clarity & tests (1–5): quality of PR + tests.
- Communication efficiency (1–5): async clarity, concise threads.
- Ownership & follow-through (1–5): completes assigned micro-project without prompting.
- Cross-team empathy (1–5): anticipates downstream impact.
- Risk awareness (1–5): surfaces known unknowns and mitigation.
Guidance: a score average <3 flags a 30-day support plan; any 1 in Ownership or Communication triggers a manager conversation.

Sample peer comment template (one line):
"Signal: good at breaking down the bug; needs to add more test cases; pairing was smooth. Recommend conditional acceptance with 30-day focused mentoring on testing patterns."

Manager 30-day acceptance decision matrix (quick)
- Accept: Evidence log + rubric average >=4 and deliverables on track.
- Conditional: rubric avg 3–4 OR 1 low score in non-critical area. Action: 2-week focused learning tasks + weekly check-ins.
- Reassess (probation): avg <3 OR Ownership=1. Action: 30-day improvement plan with clear exit criteria.

Onboarding changes to reduce friction (notes to self)
- Prepackage a "mini environment" repo with a single runnable example to generate the immediate confidence signal.
- Create a single shared Confluence page per transfer containing 5 links not 20.
- Use a standard slack channel naming convention: #reboard-<name>-<team>.

Unresolved questions / tradeoffs
- How to standardize when role requires additional security approvals (HSM, KMS)? Current playbook points to Security policy but adds delay.
- For contractor-to-perm, do we require an extra formal interview panel or can evidence log + rubric suffice? Tradeoff: speed vs calibration.

Quick templates (copy-paste)
1) 30-day priorities (manager template):
- Priority A (first 14 days): [short description]
- Priority B (14–30 days): [short description]
- Risk: [top 1] and mitigation plan

2) Peer rubric comment (one-liner):
- "Observed: [strength]. Opportunity: [single improvement]. Recommendation: [accept|conditional|retrain]."

3) Slack intro script (for manager):
- "Hey everyone, please welcome <name> who joined <team> today as <role>. Priya is pairing with Maya this week on a small staging deploy—please ping the channel if you have context to share."

Archive & follow-up
- Create a single transfer doc under team folder: team/transfers/<name>-reboard-YYYYMMDD. Add the evidence log, rubric excerpts, and the 30-day decision.
- Set calendar reminders for 15- and 30-day manager review.

Appendix: quick links to helpful artifacts
- internal transfers playbook (Confluence) — see linked_artifacts
- sample micro-project list (team repo) — request from mentor
- contractor conversion checklist (people-ops template)

Notes: draft stage — expecting feedback from Maya and Ben on simplifying rubric to 3 items max. Will pilot with 4 transfers in Q1 2026.

End of doc
